rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes adding Ti to form TiC particles during spark plasma sintering, whereas the paper uses liquid-metal dealloying in molten Cu to selectively replace Ti-rich interdendritic regions. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies spark plasma sintering and high heat flux (~10 MW/m²) up to ~1000 °C, while the paper uses vacuum-sealed silica ampoules at 1200 °C for 96 h and measures thermal conductivity from room temperature to 800 °C. The processing and testing regimes are entirely different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes TiC particle pinning to suppress void coalescence and phase separation, whereas the paper's mechanism relies on preferential Ti dissolution into Cu, immiscibility-driven retention of W/Ta/V ligaments, and a W-rich passivating interlayer. These are different classes of mechanism.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved thermal conductivity relative to an untreated W–Cu composite, while the paper predicts and measures a substantial increase in thermal conductivity for the RHEA–Cu composite relative to the WTaVTi precursor, surpassing pure W at high temperature. The property and direction are broadly similar, but the specific comparison and magnitude differ.
